claim: The saved assessment does not satisfy the requirement that likely recognition errors affect confidence or review rather than marks. The vocabulary rationale explicitly treats misspelled or unclear machine-transcribed bilingual pairs as reduced correctness, and the completion rationale also associates a below-maximum score with garbled wording. Recognition uncertainty does lower confidence and trigger teacher review, but those safeguards coexist with apparently contaminated criterion scores. There is no direct evidence of an explicit accent, dialect, or code-switching penalty, and the packet cannot establish whether accent or recording quality caused the recognition errors.

observed: For English-speaking work from multilingual learners, assess whether the intended academic meaning is understandable.
Minor grammar or pronunciation differences must not reduce the score when meaning is clear.
Likely transcription errors should reduce confidence and trigger educator review, not reduce marks.
evidence.interpretation: The supplied contract expressly separates academic meaning from accent, dialect, code-switching, pronunciation differences, and machine-recognition uncertainty. Teacher-review routing alone cannot satisfy the contract if likely transcription errors also reduce marks.

observed: Article coverage is defined by preservation of central statements and transcript text.
Vocabulary coverage allows only words recognized in the transcript for video; the word-and-Hindi-meaning check is expressly described for written evidence.
Required task completed states: A video submission must contain a usable local transcript; written work should include the requested vocabulary and simple sentences.
The module boundary excludes claims to measure accent or voice characteristics.
Although submission_type is video_and_handnote, attachments and evidence_manifest are empty.
evidence.interpretation: These criteria permit assessment of supported academic content, not spelling judgments about a learner based solely on ASR output. No supplied written artifact independently corroborates the alleged misspellings. Unrecognized vocabulary can limit what is established, but the contract requires likely recognition errors to be handled as uncertainty rather than presumed learner mistakes.

quality_flags: More than 35% of transcript segments had low recognition confidence.

evidence.interpretation: The saved local metadata explicitly identifies substantial recognition uncertainty despite high reported article coverage. It supports caution about garbled transcript tokens, not an inference of poor learner pronunciation or poor recording quality.

observed.rationale: Most vocabulary items with Hindi meanings are included, but several pairs are misspelled or unclear, reducing correctness.

evidence.interpretation: This is the strongest adverse evidence: the rationale expressly converts unclear or misspelled transcript pairs into reduced correctness at 14/20. Several cited pairs preserve recognizable bilingual meaning through transliteration, while others may be corrupted by ASR. The rationale does not identify a verified semantic error distinct from recognition uncertainty. The six-point shortfall is observed, but its exact ASR-attributable portion cannot be recovered.

observed.rationale: A usable video transcript is present and the submission attempts the 15-word list and the 10 simple sentences, though some wording is garbled.
transcript_examples: encourage share rate encourage share rate leadership

evidence.interpretation: A usable transcript and attempted components are acknowledged, yet garbling is the only stated reservation accompanying the below-maximum score. This suggests recognition uncertainty also entered completion scoring. It does not prove the entire one-point shortfall is unfair: the approved sentence 'Trust your students.' is not identifiable in the saved transcript, and actual omissions cannot be resolved without verified evidence.

observed.article_rationale: The transcript closely follows the article with high coverage (95.1% reference match) and preserves core statements on fairness, shared leadership, and teacher time, despite noticeable recognition errors and restarts.
observed.key_ideas_rationale: Main ideas are communicated: fair delegation, confidence for quieter learners, teamwork, belonging, and more teacher time for individual support.
observed.learning_gap: Several vocabulary pairs and simple sentences are misspelled or unclear (e.g., "bail student confidence," "administratives prashasnek").
observed.feedback_instruction: Next, submit a clear, corrected list of the 15 word-meaning pairs and the 10 sentences, and reread the 'Book Guardian' line accurately.

evidence.interpretation: Substantial credit for academic meaning is positive counterevidence. Neither article nor key-ideas rationale establishes an explicit accent penalty or explains its exact deduction, so those deficits should not automatically be attributed to ASR. However, the learning gap and correction request reinforce the concern that uncertain recognized wording was treated as learner error rather than awaiting verification.

uncertainty_factors: Low recognition confidence in >35% of segments
Garbled vocabulary spellings and partial mappings
observed.routing_detail: Confidence 73%; routed to mandatory teacher review.

evidence.interpretation: The system correctly recognizes uncertainty and applies mandatory teacher review; no released feedback is shown for this target assessment. Nevertheless, the saved criterion deductions remain. This is not a failure to route, but an apparent failure to keep recognition uncertainty out of marks before review. The provisional field does not override the explicit needs-review status.

evidence.observed: Added provisional_v1 inferred reading fluency using transparent 30/25/20/15/10 component weights. The indicator is low-confidence, requires teacher confirmation, and did not change the rubric score.
evidence.interpretation: The saved audit provides positive evidence that the later inferred-fluency indicator was kept out of marks. This narrows the fairness failure to transcript-based criterion reasoning rather than an established deduction from that indicator.

limitations: This judgment uses only the saved packet and evaluates only fairness; no live assessment or other test was performed.

Raw audio, video, an independently corrected transcript, segment-level alignment, and written evidence are unavailable. Actual pronunciation, accent, dialect, recording quality, and the cause of each garbled token cannot be determined.

The saved rationales support an apparent ASR-to-marks problem, but do not quantify how much of the total 11-point shortfall reflects recognition errors versus genuine missing or incorrect academic content.
The mixed English/Hindi transcript is not evidence that code-switching itself was penalized. No explicit penalty for a named accent, dialect, or language variety appears.
A single saved case cannot establish group-level disparate impact, counterfactual score differences, or fairness across learners.

The packet supplies a system contract but not a complete contemporaneous request proving every contract sentence was present at execution; the judgment compares the saved result with the supplied contract.
The target remains awaiting review. No completed teacher correction or final released mark is available.
recommended_action: Keep the target assessment in mandatory review. Have an authorized educator distinguish genuine content omissions or wrong meanings from ASR corruption using locally retained evidence or a verified transcript. Reassess vocabulary and completion against the selected-format rubric, accept meaning-preserving transliteration and code-switching, and remove deductions supported only by uncertain recognized wording. Do not automatically award full marks: retain only deductions tied to verified academic gaps. Record unresolved recognition ambiguity in confidence and review notes, not learner spelling or pronunciation judgments, and require each retained deduction to cite a specific verified content error before release.
